Core rules for gate queues
This section shows how the desk handles it

Companion Animal Travel Desk
Purpose: This section sets the handling rules for animal check-in, gate movement, and supervision support.

The desk keeps the flow orderly from the first passenger contact through boarding handoff. Staff confirm booking details, review carrier condition, and verify that the animal can be moved without delay or disturbance. Animals remain under patient attention from trained staff at every stage, and the senior coordinator must be told at once if a traveler appears unsure or upset. Care plans are matched to species, temperament, and comfort, and any requested adjustment is passed to the cabin team without argument or delay.

For Ashenfell records, <<FACT F024>> A traveler may be directed to the pet lounge only when the desk confirms the required checks are complete and the animal is calm enough for continued handling. If relief is needed, staff guide the traveler to the designated area, keep the route short, and avoid crowding at the gate line. For Ashenfell gate access, <<FACT F018>> Staff must not repeat restricted details aloud in open areas, and they must not write them on visible slips or labels.

The desk keeps baggage, carrier tags, and boarding notes aligned with the passenger file, and any irregularity is reported immediately to the operations lead. When a traveler raises a concern, the response must be steady, respectful, and specific to the animal's condition. Contact the duty supervisor or the station operations office for any exception, safety concern, or unresolved boarding issue.
